text:
Minnesota arrives on a small sting: the Wild's three-game winning streak ended with a 4-3 overtime loss to the Islanders, even though they are 3-1-1 in their last five. They are missing Jared Spurgeon, Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno. Washington has won three straight, most recently 4-3 at Nashville, and is without Vincent Desharnais. Our numbers say Minnesota is better than its record: it has a +12 goal difference, but has scored 11.9 fewer goals than its chances usually produce, so finishing has cost it.

The teams are close in chance creation at five on five. Minnesota has taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Washington 53%. Special teams offer the sharper contrast: the Wild's power play creates 0.94 expected goals a game against a Capitals penalty kill that allows 0.82, and Washington takes 4.3 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Jesper Wallstedt (+8.6 goals saved above expected this season) and Logan Thompson (+5.0, after +28.2 last season) both come in strong, and Wallstedt was at +5.8 last year.

Kirill Kaprizov is the player to watch, with a 51% chance to score and a 4-game point streak, one point from 500 career points. As Michael Russo of The Athletic posted, there is a "78-goal pace" to discuss. Matt Boldy also has a 43% chance to score. For Washington, Alex Tuch has 10 goals in 12 games, but we put his chance at 36%.
